adequacy_evidence.quote: **Scientific adequacy: qualified.** The group analysis supports the narrow reported outcome under its stated independent-participant, symmetric-null and fixed-upstream-map assumptions. The maximum-t sign-flip procedure provides whole-brain family-wise control if participant effects are sign-symmetric under the null; the report states this assumption, but does not diagnose it. The atlas-defined medial-frontal/subcallosal ROI is a reasonable independent vmPFC proxy with an orbital-frontal sensitivity mask, but cannot represent every vmPFC boundary. Missing first-level variance maps also limit precision weighting and variance-component modeling. These qualifications do not overturn the report's appropriately conditional conclusion.

hypothesis_conclusion.quote: The supplied gain-effect maps do **not** support a positive gain response in vmPFC under whole-brain family-wise error (FWE) control.
